decisions.reason: As a newly introduced and still rolling-out specialist product with no clear negative market signal yet, it would likely be kept while management uses slack to learn whether performance reaches aspirations.

This is a close-to-core dosimetry product and, absent evidence of clear underperformance, a German precision-instrument firm would usually keep it on the market for another year to assess adoption against aspirations.
Although it overlaps with other chamber launches, there is no sign yet that results fall below aspiration levels enough to trigger dropping rather than continued evaluation.
A standard clinical ionization chamber fits the firm’s established competence and portfolio logic, so management would be unlikely to remove it quickly without strong evidence of shortfall.

Because it extends the firm’s radiation-measurement range and no failure signal is visible, boundedly rational management would likely retain it while monitoring whether it meets niche-market aspirations.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional adjacent offering, and with no observed below-aspiration outcome the product would probably be kept rather than withdrawn.
